title: Jack Pettis's band and a year of New York vaudeville
summary: Hazel lists the players in Pettis's band, and says they worked vaudeville for over a year about 1929-30.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And you don't remember who was in Pettis's band by the chance.

Tony, like I told you, Tony Perrani. And, uh, we had a carnet jazz carnet player, a guy by the name, uh, uh, he had played with, boy he was a jig, but he, he played with all, he was white as you are. Uh, Nigga Moore was his name. He was famous for his hat, you know, the, the derby with the growling, you know. He, he was famous for that. And then we had a kid out of Whiteman's band, Frankie Cush, played lead. Trompett, didn't, in those days he never had no five brass, he only had three brass. Uh, Charlie Butterfield on, on trombone. And, uh, his brother Walter, saxophone. And, uh, uh, Chubby McGrath, uh, Chubby McGrath, uh, Fulton McGrath is his right name. You might, you know him, he's done, he played with Goodman and all those guys in the swing area. He was on piano. And, Bonnie Pottle on bass. And the guitar player was from New Orleans, but I can't, I can't think of his name. Wasn't Jack Kuhn. Oh. Johnny Plant. He played, played viola and he played guitar and banjo. He was on, on that band. And, uh, I'm trying to think of the other saxophone players. It was a regular, vaudeville like. That's all we did, we played vaudeville. And, uh, had dance team, you know, and a comedian. A regular unit, you know, a whole unit. And we played, we played around New York. Without even leaving New York, we played over a year. That, that's how much vaudeville had going in those days.
About what year was that, do you remember?

I think that was, it was either, either 29 or 30, Bill. Because I went up there at the latter part of 27. And I think that was, and I, I worked over this, this laundry for seven, eight months or better. And, uh, and then I went with Pettis.
